messages.subject: multiple group bfactor - focal group hyperparameters for G
parts:
Hi, 

I can't tell if this forum is for help with mirt or penis envy. I'm seeing more evidence of the latter, but hoping for the former.

I am not sure if this behavior is expected with the bfactor function when performing multiple groups analysis. I am finding that only the mean -- not the variance -- of the general factor in the focal group is being estimated. I was expecting both of these hyperparameters to be freed. Reprex shown below, based on some of the example code from ?bfactor.

Thanks

library(mirt)
#> Loading required package: stats4
#> Loading required package: lattice



### load SAT12 and compute bifactor model with 3 specific factors
data(SAT12)
data <- key2binary(SAT12,
                   key = c(1,4,5,2,3,1,2,1,3,1,2,4,2,1,5,3,4,4,1,4,3,3,4,1,3,5,1,3,1,5,4,5))
specific <- c(2,3,2,3,3,2,1,2,1,1,1,3,1,3,1,2,1,1,3,3,1,1,3,1,3,3,1,3,2,3,1,2)
set.seed(456)
group <- sample(c("G1", "G2"), nrow(data), replace = TRUE)
data <- data.frame(data)
mod1 <- bfactor(data, specific,
                group = group,
                invariance = c("free_means", "free_vars", names(data)),
                technical = list(NCYCLES = 5000),
                verbose = FALSE)
sapply(coef(mod1, printSE = TRUE), "[", "GroupPars")
#> $G1.GroupPars
#>     MEAN_1 MEAN_2 MEAN_3 MEAN_4 COV_11 COV_21 COV_31 COV_41 COV_22 COV_32
#> par      0      0      0      0      1      0      0      0      1      0
#>     COV_42 COV_33 COV_43 COV_44
#> par      0      1      0      1
#>
#> $G2.GroupPars
#>         MEAN_1 MEAN_2 MEAN_3 MEAN_4 COV_11 COV_21 COV_31 COV_41 COV_22 COV_32
#> par 0.08768718      0      0      0      1      0      0      0      1      0
#>     COV_42 COV_33 COV_43 COV_44
#> par      0      1      0      1

I am not sure if this behavior is expected with the bfactor function when performing multiple groups analysis. I am finding that only the mean -- not the variance -- of the general factor in the focal group is being estimated. I was expecting both of these hyperparameters to be freed. Reprex shown below, based on some of the example code from ?bfactor.
Looks to have been a specification bug as it works when 'free_var' works rather than 'free_vars'. I've sent a patch to the dev, and this is what the new output looks like:
> sapply(coef(mod1, printSE = TRUE), "[", "GroupPars")

$G1.GroupPars
    MEAN_1 MEAN_2 MEAN_3 MEAN_4 COV_11 COV_21 COV_31 COV_41 COV_22 COV_32 COV_42 COV_33
par      0      0      0      0      1      0      0      0      1      0      0      1
    COV_43 COV_44
par      0      1

$G2.GroupPars
        MEAN_1 MEAN_2 MEAN_3 MEAN_4   COV_11 COV_21 COV_31 COV_41 COV_22 COV_32 COV_42
par 0.09296939      0      0      0 1.071053      0      0      0      1      0      0
    COV_33 COV_43 COV_44
par      1      0      1


Thanks for letting me know, and sorry for the poor spam filters.

Phil
